html:
SMTO-RST-0004 — This conversation changed while SMTO was saving

GUID: 399996ff-498b-44fc-bc21-194ed6631de8
Slug: run-journal-revision-conflict
Domain: RST · Subsystem: rst

What happened

  • Something else added to this conversation while SMTO was saving an update, such as another task or another window. SMTO didn't save the update, so it wouldn't overwrite the newer messages.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and open the conversation again. Reloading shows the messages that were added while this update was being saved.
  2. Check whether another task in this conversation, or the same conversation in another window, is still working, and let it finish. Two things writing to one conversation at the same moment cause this conflict.
  3. Then send your message or continue the task again, if it's still needed. Once you're working from the latest messages, the save can go through.

What success looks like

  • Your new message appears after the latest ones and no messages are missing.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Until it's sorted out, use the conversation in only one window.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A run save supplied an expected journal position that differs from the current retained message count, because another writer appended to the conversation journal first.

What this means

  • A save supplies expected journal position and the authoritative retained message count differs from it. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • A save supplies expected journal position and the authoritative retained message count differs from it.

How to diagnose it

  • Reload the authoritative journal head and current run owner before merging any update.

How to fix it

  • Reload the authoritative conversation journal head and check its current run owner, then save against the current journal_end; do not resubmit a stale journal position after another writer changed the journal (MemoryRunStore._save / RunStore.save_in).
  • Reload the authoritative conversation journal head and reconcile its current run owner before saving again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported save uses the current exact head and preserves intervening messages.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
